## d1dab66b0d54

**Reproduced semantic distribution defect; audited source unchanged.**  The
canonical rule always shifts every red cell in the positive direction by the
spacing between sorted green anchors.  The generator's vertical branch places
the red line on row `h-2` or `h-1`, then the canonical rule shifts it down by
2–3 rows; the horizontal branch analogously places it at the right edge and
shifts it right.  Thus ordinary generated movers are erased as out-of-bounds
instead of translated.

For seed 17, sample indices 0–3, all four generated pairs lose every red cell:
input/output red counts are `3/0`, `2/0`, `2/0`, and `2/0`.  The retained first
counterexample has green anchors `(0,3)` and `(3,3)`, red cells on row 4, and
canonical shift `(3,0)`; all three landings are outside its 6×8 grid.  The
supported `arcpuzzles apply --check-generator-domain` command executes canonical
Racket and reports the input as generator-domain `valid`, exposing that
`self_check` does not enforce the declared in-bounds invariant.

The grammar is also far from canonical support: generated pairs use exactly two
green anchors and a 1-D red line, while the four canonical pairs contain 4–9
greens forming a dotted guide and eight red cells forming a 3×3 ring around one
green.  A model can therefore learn the trivial “erase red” behavior rather than
the intended translation relation.

This finding is bound to generator SHA-256
`f7e1847e0e60c52fe09ee6146d56b95af983f13910240d9084b1fe7b29a909ba`
and canonical executed rule hash `76783c197f4d`.  I did not modify this target.
